# Spec Reconciliation & Feature Truthfulness Requirements Quality Checklist: Playable Compost Loop

**Purpose**: Requirements quality review checklist assessing English specification clarity, completeness, consistency, and boundary guardrails for spec reconciliations, feature claim truthfulness, conflict overrides, and spike boundaries in Feature 004.
**Created**: 2026-10-04
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Document Reconciliation Scope & Boundaries

- [x] CHK001 Does the specification enumerate the exact set or provide unambiguous identification criteria for the "all eight currently stale specification and plan documents" requiring multiplayer scope reconciliation? [Completeness, Spec §FR-017]
- [x] CHK002 Are the editing boundaries for stale document reconciliation defined with concrete guardrails that prohibit reopening or redesigning settled requirements? [Clarity/Consistency, Spec §FR-017, §Assumptions]
- [x] CHK003 Does the specification define an unambiguous criterion for what constitutes a constitutional contradiction versus a valid feature-scoped multiplayer limitation? [Clarity, Spec §FR-017, §SC-007, §User Story 4]
- [x] CHK004 Is the relationship between Feature 004's scope reconciliation and future multiplayer roadmapped work items explicitly demarcated to prevent scope leakage? [Boundary/Consistency, Spec §FR-017, §Assumptions]

## Feature Claim Truthfulness & Observability

- [x] CHK005 Is the target document and location of the "project's user-facing feature list" uniquely and unambiguously identified? [Completeness/Clarity, Spec §FR-016, §SC-006, §User Story 4]
- [x] CHK006 Is the criteria for determining whether a feature claim is "observable in the game" defined with concrete, verifiable standards rather than subjective wording? [Measurability, Spec §FR-016, §User Story 4 Scenarios]
- [x] CHK007 Does the specification define the mandatory syntax, format, or taxonomy required when a capability must be "explicitly labelled as not yet working"? [Consistency/Clarity, Spec §FR-016, §User Story 4]
- [x] CHK008 Are all existing unverified or planned features currently described in project documentation identified or bounded so reviewer audit scope is clear? [Coverage, Spec §FR-016, §SC-006]

## Conflict & Override Specification Clarity

- [x] CHK009 Is the retirement of the 1–5 compost maturation multiplier stated with clear supersession language specifying what earlier specification rules are overridden? [Clarity/Consistency, Spec §Clarifications, §FR-005a, §Assumptions]
- [x] CHK010 Is the override regarding removed bin retention (retaining contents and progress instead of dropping items on the ground) explicitly specified with complete boundary conditions against the legacy specification? [Consistency/Clarity, Spec §FR-005c, §Assumptions]
- [x] CHK011 Is the inheritance boundary for organic waste qualification completely specified, clearly stating how external changes to that qualification set affect Feature 004? [Completeness, Spec §Clarifications, §FR-003, §Assumptions]
- [x] CHK012 Is the unresolved divergence regarding artisan goods exclusion documented with explicit rationale and non-regression boundaries so implementers do not inadvertently alter it? [Clarity/Edge Cases, Spec §Assumptions]

## Spike & Assumption Boundaries

- [x] CHK013 Does the specification provide clear success/failure exit criteria and fallbacks for the initial item registration spike without content-patching dependencies? [Boundary/Clarity, Spec §Assumptions]
- [x] CHK014 Are the assumed capabilities of the game's native machine interface specified with fallback or escalation paths if native interface discovery fails to meet requirements? [Clarity/Risk, Spec §FR-001a, §Assumptions]
- [x] CHK015 Is the verification gap between single-player testing availability and multiplayer correctness requirements formally bounded with clear acceptance criteria? [Completeness/Measurability, Spec §Assumptions, §SC-010]
- [x] CHK016 Are the boundaries between placeholder assets/i18n and functional game-native messaging explicitly specified to prevent unneeded asset or UI development? [Scope/Clarity, Spec §FR-008a, §Assumptions]

## Measurability of Project Signal Quality

- [x] CHK017 Is the verification methodology for SC-006 ("Zero user-facing feature claims in the project are false or unlabelled") defined with measurable, objective audit steps? [Measurability, Spec §SC-006, §User Story 4]
- [x] CHK018 Is the audit check for SC-007 ("Zero specification or plan documents declare multiplayer support out of scope in contradiction of the project's constitution") verifiable via a deterministic checklist or procedure? [Measurability, Spec §SC-007, §FR-017]
- [x] CHK019 Are the acceptance criteria for concurrent interaction refusal clearly defined with expected player-visible feedback mechanisms? [Measurability/Coverage, Spec §FR-008a, §FR-019, §SC-010]
- [x] CHK020 Does the specification define measurable verification criteria for ensuring that removing and restoring a bin cannot be exploited to duplicate compost or alter processing progress? [Measurability/Edge Cases, Spec §FR-005b, §FR-005c, §SC-009]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- Add comments or findings inline
- Link to relevant resources or documentation
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference
